plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A graceful ornamental tree that produces masses of pale pink to white five-petaled flowers before its leaves emerge. Peak bloom in many temperate regions creates dramatic canopies of blossom that drift down as petals in the wind.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere; later in colder northern Japan and high elevations
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. USA, Korea, and temperate parks and gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: The famous cherry trees around the Tidal Basin in Washington D.C. were a 1912 gift from Tokyo, and most of them are Yoshino cherries.

plants.name: Tulipa gesneriana
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with cup-shaped flowers on sturdy stems above blue-green strap-like leaves. Hundreds of cultivars exist, with forms ranging from single and double to fringed and parrot types.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-April to early May in the Netherlands and much of northern Europe and North America
plants.location: Netherlands, Turkey, Central Asia origins; widely cultivated across temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: During the Dutch 'Tulip Mania' of the 1630s, single bulbs sold for more than the price of a luxury canal house.

plants.name: Cercis canadensis
plants.description: A small deciduous tree whose bare branches and even trunks are covered in clusters of magenta-pink pea-like flowers in spring, followed by heart-shaped leaves. It is a favorite early nectar source for native bees.
plants.location: Eastern and central United States, woodland edges and understory, extending to northern Mexico
plants.funFact: Redbud flowers are edible and have a mildly tart flavor; they grow directly from the bark through a trait called cauliflory.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall tropical and subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that bursts into clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers. In regions where it has a second bloom, flowering can occur in autumn.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn bloom (March to April) in parts of the Southern Hemisphere, such as some areas of southern Africa and Australia; main bloom in spring elsewhere
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa, Australia, Brazil, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, thousands of jacarandas line the streets, earning it the nickname 'Jacaranda City'.
